svg.font-family: 'Comic Sans MS', 'Chalkboard SE', 'Comic Neue', 'Bradley Hand', casual, sans-serif
svg.title: Receiver: from the pads to two 32-bit words
svg.desc: rx_p / rx_n go through rx_term (100 ohm differential, reference vtt), ctle (peaking equalizer) and vga (gain set by vctrl). The output afe_p / afe_n feeds 24 slicers and rx_cdr. The slicers are two groups of 12: phase 0 samples on clk14 rising, phase 1 on clk14 falling. Each group is 3 thresholds (+100, 0, -100 mV) times 4 guesses of the previous symbol (-3, -1, +1, +3). dfe1_unrolled_hr drives the 24 slicer references and, per phase, keeps the 3 outputs whose guess matches the previous symbol. One pam4_dec per phase turns the 3 bits into an MSB and an LSB, and one rx_dec_retime per phase retimes them. Each binary path then has an rx_deser_path: 2 lanes at 14 Gb/s, 2 demux2_cml on clk7 give 4 at 7, 4 demux2_cml on clk3p5 give 8 at 3.5, a CML to CMOS conversion, 8 demux2_cmos on clk1p75 give 16 at 1.75, 16 demux2_cmos on clk0p875 give 32 at 0.875, and an output register on clk0p875 gives rxd_m[0:31] or rxd_l[0:31].

g.text: Receiver: from the pads to two 32-bit words
Half rate: the rising edges of clk14 sample every other symbol (phase 0), the falling edges the ones between (phase 1).
phase 0, clk14 rising: 3 thresholds (rows) x 4 guesses of the previous symbol (columns)
rx_deser_path one binary path. There are two:
the MSB path gives rxd_m, the LSB path gives rxd_l.
one lane from each phase: this path's bit
Two 32-bit words per rx_wclk cycle (0.875 GHz).
Bit j is time slot j; slot 0 was received first.
CMOS on one side, CML on the other
